newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin says "one country, two systems" and "principle of Hong Kong people governing Hong Kong" and a high degree of autonomy toward Hong Kong is China's long-term policy.
- Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji meets U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan, and says hopes central banks of two countries would increase exchanges and cooperation.
- Vice-Premier and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen tells visiting Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi that China attaches great importance to relations with Malaysia
- State Technical Supervision Bureau finds only 76.2 percent of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region badges and flags reach quality standards
- State Council appoints Li Hong as director of State Statistal Bureau
- President Jiang Zemin says fight on desertification, environmental protection, economic development and poverty elimination are tough and urgent tasks

- Recent years have seen smooth growth of relations between China and Vietnam, and frequent exchanges of high-level visits, Politburo member Li Ruihuan tells Le Quang Dao, president of the Central Committee of the Vietnam Fatherland Front
Bank of China to increase domestic loans by 50 billion yuan this year, foreign exchange loans by $2.2 billion
- Washing machine giant Rongshida sees top output in 1995 and 1996 and production increases 10.22 percent in first quarter
- Beijing plans to use three years to curb dangers in subway
- New concept of family doctors who treat patients in homes and neighbourhoods launched in some major cities.
- Two sides of Sino-British Joint Liaison Group reach agreement on China sending two more advance parties of People's Liberation Army garrison to Hong Kong
